title: Answer: intelligence is what a system can do, conceptually distinct from consciousness

statements.text: Seth takes intelligence, as a working definition, to be what a system can do: in Legg and Hutter's words, the ability to achieve goals in a wide range of environments. Reasoning, planning and language are aspects of it, but animals without them can still behave intelligently. Intelligence and consciousness are conceptually distinct, since a system could behave intelligently with nothing it is like to be it, and the reverse, though in practice the two may not be independent.
statements.scope: Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism (2025, accepted manuscript)
